html:
The Belitung shipwreck is an Arab dhow that sank around 830 CE off Belitung Island, between Sumatra and Borneo, on its way home from China. Its cargo was the largest find of Tang dynasty goods ever made in one place.

Fishermen found it in 1998. The ship was built in the western Indian Ocean of planks sewn together with rope, without nails. It carried about 60,000 pieces of Chinese ceramics, most of them bowls from the Changsha kilns, packed in jars, along with fine gold and silver objects and bronze mirrors. Some bowls bear Arabic style patterns and Quranic phrases, made to suit buyers in the Abbasid world.

The wreck is proof of a direct sea trade between China and the Persian Gulf in the 800s, along what is now called the Maritime Silk Road, with the straits controlled by Srivijaya. It was raised by a commercial salvage firm and the cargo was sold to Singapore, now shown at the Asian Civilisations Museum. Archaeologists criticised the quick salvage, and some museums refused to exhibit it.
sum: The Belitung shipwreck is an Arab dhow that sank around 830 CE off Belitung Island, between Sumatra and Borneo, on its way home from China. Its cargo was the largest find of Tang dynasty goods ever made in one place.
